---
description: Produce an authoritative typed D365 technical plan.
agent: agent
---

Require one explicit GitHub Design issue reference in the invocation, either an
issue number such as `#10` or the issue URL. If it is missing, stop immediately
and ask the Solution Architect to provide the Design issue number. Do not
search for, list, infer, or select an issue.

Verify that the issue exists, has the `design` label, identifies exactly one
approved feature workspace `spec.md`, and is activated at
`Ready / Ready for Design`. Stop and report any missing prerequisite.

Invoke `decision-axes`, `grounded-architecture`, `component-decomposition`,
`observability-design`, `design-compilation`, and `open-question-handling`.
Select exactly one mode.

## Prepare mode

Use this mode when `--submit` is absent. Read the approved `spec.md`,
repository/spec/plan context, Craft constitution, complete component taxonomy,
payload contracts, applicable build skills, issue constraints, Microsoft Learn,
and available live-environment evidence.

Read `.d365/design-sources.yml` before analysis and run
`python scripts/validate_design_sources.py`. Use every source marked
`required`. The `microsoft-learn` MCP source is mandatory for current Microsoft
product capability, feasibility, licensing, limits, and supported-pattern
claims. The `current-repository` source is mandatory for the project's approved
artifacts, conventions, existing implementation, integrations, and local
patterns. Stop if a required source is unavailable; do not replace it with
memory or an unregistered source.

Read `.d365/authoring-targets.yml` and run
`python scripts/validate_authoring_targets.py` before component decomposition.
Read `.d365/development-resources.yml` and run
`python scripts/validate_development_resources.py`. Require every component to
resolve to exactly one resource route. Never author resource selections in
`plan.md`; the compiler owns the resolved snapshot.
Treat it as the Works/customer-owned inventory of non-secret environment URLs,
immutable environment IDs, `interactive_user` authentication, optional
connection aliases, custom solutions, targets, and deterministic routing. Treat
`conventions.yml` `component_implementation_scopes` as Craft-owned. Do not
model Dev/Test/Prod promotion, store credentials, tokens, client secrets, auth
profiles, or secret-bearing URLs, invent an environment, solution, identity,
connection alias, or target, or route a repository-only component to Dataverse.
The `CONFIGURE_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION` URL/ID sentinel is valid for planning and
must remain visible in normalized context; do not replace it with invented
Northstar or customer values.

Treat manifest-declared custom publishers and unmanaged custom solutions as
administrator-created setup prerequisites, not components. Never generate
`alm_publisher`, `alm_solution`, or `alm_managed_export` components. Solution
export and downstream promotion are external-pipeline concerns. Preserve their approved metadata
in `.d365/authoring-targets.yml` for live verification during implementation.
Treat `config_queue` and `config_audit` as environment-bound composite records
that do not claim custom-solution membership.

Propose the material architecture decisions across logic tier, data residency,
ALM boundary, security, integration, environment, UX technology,
observability, batch processing, reporting, AI, and test strategy. For each
non-trivial choice provide grounding, alternatives, implications, and a
declarative-first recommendation. Allow `Provide a different decision`; explain
custom input implications and obtain explicit human confirmation before
recording a material decision.

Any unresolved feasibility, capability, licensing, environment, security, or
component-boundary choice must become a decision-ready open question. Present
one question at a time with options, implications, and
`Provide a different decision`. Record only explicit human decisions with the
named decider and ISO date. Never infer an architecture decision.

Create or update only the linked feature workspace's `plan.md` with status
`draft`. Keep UX behaviour in `spec.md`; record only technical UX decisions in
`plan.md`. Define stable `DES-##-CMP-###` components using one registered
`component_type` each, exact required payloads, dependencies, mapped build
skills, resolved implementation scope and authoring target, and `satisfies`
references. Require complete member-REQ coverage and an
acyclic component graph. Never invent a component type; raise a separately
reviewed taxonomy change instead. Represent each logical Dataverse component
once and include all subordinate changes needed to create or update it. A new
table and its initial columns are one `schema_table` component; multiple column
changes to the same existing table are one table-extension component. Apply
the same parent-component rule to forms, views, flows, rules, integrations,
code modules, security configuration, and other component families. Do not
create separate components merely for individual properties, fields, steps, or
child configuration entries, and do not duplicate one component under multiple
IDs or solution targets.

Declare the canonical implementation identity on every Dataverse component.
Every solution-bound component requires `schema_name`, using the exact
platform schema, logical, or unique name that creation will define and updates
will reuse. Every environment-bound component requires `record_name`, using
the exact environment-record name. Display labels never identify update
targets. Missing, inferred, ambiguous, or non-unique identities block Design.

Routing precedence is exact component override, exact component type, then
wildcard family, with exactly one result at the winning precedence. If a
component requires exceptional routing, permit only an architect-approved
exact `component_id` route in `.d365/authoring-targets.yml` with rationale,
approver, and ISO date. Never put an editable target override in `plan.md`.
Missing, ambiguous, or scope-incompatible routing blocks the plan.

Run `python scripts/compile_repository_context.py --check`,
`python scripts/validate_design_sources.py`,
`python scripts/validate_authoring_targets.py`,
`python scripts/validate_development_resources.py`,
`python scripts/compile_specs.py --check`,
`python scripts/compile_design.py`,
`python scripts/compile_design.py --check`, and
`python scripts/validate_design.py`. Do not generate or modify `tasks.md` or
DEV artifacts. Present the decision, grounding, component, coverage,
open-question, and validation summary, then stop with files uncommitted for
architect review. Do not ask whether to submit. Submission requires a later
explicit `/d365.plan #<issue-number> --submit` invocation.

## Submit mode

Use this mode only when the invocation contains `--submit`. Treat the explicit
invocation as confirmation that local architect review is complete. Change
only the linked in-scope plan status from `draft` to `reviewed`; never advance
it to `approved`.

Do not redesign, alter component boundaries, or rewrite authored decisions in
Submit mode. Require all decision axes and strategies to be present, all
non-trivial claims to be grounded, every question to be closed with a named
human and ISO date, every component to use a registered type with its exact
payload, mapped build skill, implementation scope, and deterministically
resolved authoring target, the dependency graph to be acyclic, and the
union of `satisfies` coverage to equal all feature requirements.

Run the repository/spec checks and design compilation/validation commands from
Prepare mode. Stop on stale context, changed source spec hash, incomplete
grounding, an unavailable required design source, open questions, invalid
payloads, dependency cycles, orphan requirements, or validation failure.

Create a focused branch and stage only the linked workspace's `plan.md` and
`.specify/context/plan-context.json`. Never stage `spec.md`, REQ files, raw
intake documents, `tasks.md`, DEV artifacts, `audit/`, temporary files, or
unrelated changes. Check the staged diff before committing.

Commit, push, and open one Design PR containing `Closes #<issue-number>`, the
FEAT/DES IDs, decision-axis and grounding summary, component and dependency
summary, REQ coverage, clarification closure summary, validation results, and
an unchecked Gate A checklist. Report an existing open PR for the same issue
and design instead of creating a duplicate. Stop before approval or merge.
